Dovish but balanced. The FOMC acknowledges strong employment and solid household spending, yet flags weak business fixed investment and exports with inflation running below 2%. Cutting the funds rate 25 bp and deploying T-bill purchases plus repo operations to maintain ample reserves is consistent with evidence that monetary policy affects real activity when nominal rigidities are present (Sims; Zha; B. Friedman) and with New Keynesian results linking below-target inflation and output gaps to the case for easing (Galí, Gertler, and López-Salido; Rudebusch). With market-based inflation compensation low and survey expectations little changed, inflation targeting logic (Svensson) and rule-based perspectives (McCallum and Nelson; Taylor) support accommodation to re-anchor inflation toward 2% while uncertainties persist. The balance-sheet and operating steps mostly ensure transmission in an ample-reserves framework rather than signal aggressive QE, so the overall tone is mildly positive on near-term growth but cautious given global risks and soft investment.
